labels.description: The customer-facing technology risk now covers adopting AI tools and other technology innovations, adds inaccuracies and launches of new or emerging technologies as sources of disruption, and adds damage to brand and reputation as a consequence in both the headline and body.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: new exposures (AI tool adoption, inaccuracies, launches of new or emerging technologies) are disclosed, and criterion 3: the severity is widened to include brand and reputation damage.

labels.description: Political instability and geopolitical tensions are added to the list of supply chain disruption causes, while the specific COVID-19 pandemic references in the second paragraph are dropped and 'increased supply chain costs' is broadened to 'increased costs'.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: new disruption exposures (political instability, geopolitical tensions) are disclosed, and criterion 2: references to the COVID-19 pandemic as the illustrative event are dropped from the discussion of supply chain strain and online demand.

labels.description: The safety risk now names negative publicity regarding the Company and incidents such as civil unrest, raids and protests at stores or facilities, and widens the impact to store traffic and associate recruiting, while heightened shrink moves from 'have seen' to 'saw'.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: new exposures (negative publicity about the Company, civil unrest, raids, protests) are disclosed, and criterion 3: the scope of harm is widened to store traffic and associate recruiting.

labels.description: The cybersecurity risk adds that AI may enable new threat actors and novel attacks, adds South America to the conflicts raising cyber-attack risk, concedes that risk management processes may not be fully implemented or effective, and extends the regulatory discussion to AI and emerging technologies and international privacy laws.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: new risks (AI-enabled threat actors, possible ineffectiveness of cybersecurity risk management processes, compliance costs of reporting and disclosure regimes) are disclosed, and criterion 2: a new jurisdiction (South America) and new regulation categories (AI, international privacy laws) are referenced.

labels.description: Union representation is no longer attributed to associates at SRS and ongoing union organizing efforts become a hypothetical future risk ('are also subject to' becomes 'may be subject to future'), while public health concerns are replaced by safety and security in stores as a labor factor and supply chain investments are dropped from the talent-needs sentence.
labels.rationale: criterion 2: the SRS business reference and supply chain investments are dropped, and criterion 3: the union organizing risk is softened from present to hypothetical and a labor factor is swapped (public health concerns replaced by store safety and security).

labels.description: A new sentence discloses that offering new payment options may subject the company to additional rules, regulations and compliance requirements and higher fraud losses, alongside a rename of the Pro House Account trade credit program to the Pro Trade Credit program.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: a new risk (additional regulation and higher fraud losses from new payment options) is disclosed; the program rename and 'artificial intelligence' to 'AI' are minor on their own.
